examples.note: Assamese has no postalveolar affricates or fricatives; the letter জ (Indo-Aryan j) is /z/, and চ/ছ are /s/.

examples.from: Latin gentem 'people' (g before a front vowel > Early Romance [dʒ])
examples.note: The palatalized affricate fronted to [dz] and later deaffricated to [z].

preamble: Deaffrication of the voiced postalveolar affricate [dʒ] to the voiced alveolar fricative [z], which loses both the stop phase and the postalveolar place. Assamese, alone among the major Indo-Aryan languages, has no postalveolar affricates: Indo-Aryan j is pronounced [z]. Venetian likewise shows [z] where Latin had g before a front vowel, which passed through [dʒ].
